lines.trans: I am back! Here is the honey—but Rami said to smell the old book page first!
Smell an old dusty page while our best cake goes cold? That is absolute madness.
No, Salma, he is right! The paper absorbed the volatile oils from the glaze for thirty years!
Smell the paper right where the card rested for thirty years, my dear.
Close your eyes and breathe in: garden mint, sweet orange zest, and golden honey!
Of course! Warm honey stays soft and glossy without turning sour or rock hard!
And a pinch of grated orange peel brightens the summer berries without puckering Mazen!
Look at the last unsmudged word at the corner: scatter toasted sliced almonds on top.
Two spoons of warm honey, grated orange zest, and toasted almond flakes!
Tin Three is still warm on the stove rack—go brush it right now, Chef!
Do not move from that piano bench, Suad; the real cake is five minutes away!

meanings.note: The word 'رجعت' (رجعت) means 'رجعت'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: رجعت! هادا هو العسل—بس رامي حكى نشم صفحة الكتاب القديم بالأول!
examples.trans: I am back! Here is the honey—but Rami said to smell the old book page first!
This is رجعت.

examples.text: تفضلوا، هادا كتاب أعشاب الحديقة المغلف بقماش من رف مكتبة الكتب المستعملة بـ شارع الياسمين!
examples.trans: Here is the cloth-bound garden herb book from the second-hand bookshop shelf on Jasmine Street!
This is هادا.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian pronoun 'he' or 'it' (masculine).

examples.trans: He knows heritage law well.

examples.text: بيحكي هيك وهو بيطل من الشباك!
examples.trans: He says that while peeking out the window!

meanings.note: The word 'رامي' (رامي) means 'رامي'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: هادا الكتاب كان أصلا لـ رامي وعمته قبل ما يوصل لرف الإعارة!
examples.trans: This book actually belonged to Rami and his aunt before it reached the lending shelf!
This is رامي.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to speak, talk, tell' (بحكي / حكى).

examples.trans: Salma chats with all the neighbours.
Tell me everything I need to know.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: صفحات.

examples.trans: Read the second page of the letter.
The notebook fell open to the middle page.

examples.trans: Wait—do not just brush it on plain! Read the botanical book first!
This is بالأول.

examples.trans: Smell an old dusty page while our best cake goes cold? That is absolute madness.

This is الممتازة.

meanings.note: Levantine progressive marker placed before a present-tense verb to show action happening right now.

examples.trans: The water is flowing inside the pipe right now!

examples.text: كنت عم بدور على دفتري هلا.
examples.trans: I was just looking for my notebook.

meanings.note: The word 'تبرد' (تبرد) means 'تبرد'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: معنا عشر دقايق بالزبط قبل ما تبرد الكيكة وترفض أي طبقة تلميع دافية!
examples.trans: We have exactly ten minutes before the cake cools down and rejects any warm glaze!
This is تبرد.

examples.text: نشم صفحة قديمة ومغبرة وكيكتنا الممتازة عم تبرد؟ هادا جنون رسمي.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: رسمية, plural: رسميين).

examples.trans: Save the formal talk for the guests only!
An official letter arrived in the noon post.

meanings.note: Standalone لا means 'no'; before a 2nd-person subjunctive verb it forms a negative command (لا تقلقي 'do not worry!'), and لا ... ولا means 'neither ... nor'.

examples.trans: No, lift the handle first.
Do not worry, ma'am.

meanings.note: Placed directly before a name or title when addressing someone in Arabic (يا نور 'Nour!', يا أستاذ 'sir!') and in exclamations (يا سلام! 'wonderful!').

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: The word 'سلمى' (سلمى) means 'سلمى'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: خلينا ناخده طوالي لـ سلمى بغرفة تسعة قبل ما حدا يتنفس بقوة!
examples.trans: Let us carry it straight to Salma in Room Nine before anyone breathes too hard!
This is سلمى.

meanings.note: The word 'معه' (معه) means 'معه'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: لا يا سلمى، معه حق! الورق امتص الزيوت الطيارة من طبقة التلميع لمدة تلاتين سنة!
examples.trans: No, Salma, he is right! The paper absorbed the volatile oils from the glaze for thirty years!
This is معه.

meanings.note: Used in معك حق ('you are right / you have a point').

examples.trans: You are right, the weather is cold today.
Everyone has a right to rest.

meanings.note: The word 'امتص' (امتص) means 'امتص'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition meaning 'from', 'of', or 'than' after comparatives.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.

meanings.note: Used for a coat of paint (طبقة دهان), a layer of pastry, or a building storey.

examples.text: الطبقة الأولى نشفت وصارت جاهزة للطبقة التانية.
examples.trans: The first coat has dried and is ready for the second coat.

examples.text: دهان المي بيكفيه طبقتين رقيقتين عشان يطلع ناعم.
examples.trans: Water-based paint only needs two thin coats to come out smooth.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'thirty'.

examples.trans: They have given us thirty days in the letter.
The bill is thirty-eight dinars.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: سنين.

examples.trans: The building is eighty years old.
I have not seen him for three years.

meanings.note: The word 'شمي' (شمي) means 'شمي'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: شمي الورقة بالزبط محل ما كان الكرت محطوط لتلاتين سنة يا عزيزتي.
examples.trans: Smell the paper right where the card rested for thirty years, my dear.
This is شمي.

meanings.note: Signature Jordanian/Palestinian pronunciation (with z) of بالضبط ('exactly!').

examples.trans: Exactly! You have become one of us.
Tell me exactly what to buy.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian noun for any retail shop or spot (pl. محلات).

examples.trans: Below is the signature of the antique shop.
There's a pastry shop next to the house.

meanings.note: Negates verbs and في (ما بعرف 'I don't know', ما في 'there isn't'), and links conjunctions like قبل ما ('before') and بعد ما ('after').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Arabic uses no 'is/are' in the simple present, while كان supplies the past ('was/were') and يكون / بيكون supplies future or modal 'be'.

examples.trans: How was the bus ride?

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day will not be boring!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: برتقالات.

examples.trans: The fresh orange juice is cold.
We bought oranges and apples from the market.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: حلوة, plural: حلوين).

examples.trans: The strawberry jam is sweet and tasty.

examples.text: اطوي التوت الكامل شوي شوي بخليط اللوز واخبزيه أربعين دقيقة ليصير لونه ذهبي.
examples.trans: Fold whole berries gently into the almond batter and bake forty minutes until golden.
This is ذهبي.

meanings.note: Means 'certainly, definitely' or 'must be' (إنتي أكيد نور 'you must be Nour').

examples.trans: Hello! You must be Nour.

examples.text: أكيد صاحبه رح يدور عليه قريبا.
examples.trans: Surely its owner will look for it soon.

meanings.note: The word 'العسل' (العسل) means 'العسل'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.trans: Exactly, Ziad. And Tin Three gets my wild card: a thin brush of warm honey.

meanings.note: Conjunction 'or' in statements and open questions.

examples.text: مكتوب عليها اسم أو رقم تليفون؟
examples.trans: Is there a name or phone number written on it?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: قاسية, plural: قاسيين).

examples.text: كان يعمل حاله قاسي خمس ثواني بس!
examples.trans: He used to act tough for just five seconds!

meanings.note: Spoken Levantine form of مثل ('like, similar to').

examples.trans: Its color is dark blue like your suitcase!
The water is cold as ice.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ورشات.

examples.trans: There is a brass lamp in my workshop downstairs.

This is الصيف.

meanings.note: The word 'تخلي' (تخلي) means 'تخلي'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: ورشة من قشر البرتقال المبروش بتعطي نكهة لتوت الصيف من غير ما تخلي مازن يكشر!
examples.trans: And a pinch of grated orange peel brightens the summer berries without puckering Mazen!
This is تخلي.

meanings.note: The word 'مازن' (مازن) means 'مازن'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: كبست الجرس مرة واحدة فوق يا مازن، وسلكك اللطيف رن مرتين متل العادة.
examples.trans: I pressed the bell once upstairs, Mazen, and your friendly wire rang twice as usual.
This is مازن.

meanings.note: The word 'يكشر' (يكشر) means 'يكشر'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: ورشة من قشر البرتقال المبروش بتعطي نكهة لتوت الصيف من غير ما تخلي مازن يكشر!
examples.trans: And a pinch of grated orange peel brightens the summer berries without puckering Mazen!
This is يكشر.

meanings.note: Placed directly before an indefinite noun without ال- to mean 'the last' (آخر يوم 'the last day', آخر الساحة 'the far end of the courtyard').

examples.trans: The attic room is at the end of the floor.
Today is the last day of the week.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: كلمات.

examples.trans: She did not say a single word to anyone.
The word thank you warms the heart.

meanings.note: Negates nouns, adjectives, participles, and pronouns in spoken Jordanian (مش شنتتي 'not my bag', مش ملاقي 'cannot find').

examples.trans: This is not my suitcase!
Not bad for a second day at work!

meanings.note: The word 'ملطخة' (ملطخة) means 'ملطخة'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: شوفوا آخر كلمة مش ملطخة عالزاوية: رشي شرائح لوز محمصة عالوجه.
examples.trans: Look at the last unsmudged word at the corner: scatter toasted sliced almonds on top.
This is ملطخة.

meanings.note: The word 'عالزاوية' (عالزاوية) means 'عالزاوية'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: خدي جزدانك يا نور! الدكانة اللي عالزاوية جنب برج الساعة بتبيع عسل بلدي!
examples.trans: Grab your purse, Nour! The corner shop next to the clock tower sells local honey!
This is عالزاوية.

meanings.note: The word 'رشي' (رشي) means 'رشي'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: شوفوا آخر كلمة مش ملطخة عالزاوية: رشي شرائح لوز محمصة عالوجه.
examples.trans: Look at the last unsmudged word at the corner: scatter toasted sliced almonds on top.
This is رشي.

meanings.note: The word 'شرائح' (شرائح) means 'شرائح'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: شوفوا آخر كلمة مش ملطخة عالزاوية: رشي شرائح لوز محمصة عالوجه.
examples.trans: Look at the last unsmudged word at the corner: scatter toasted sliced almonds on top.
This is شرائح.

meanings.note: Collective noun for almonds (singulative لوزة).

examples.text: ريحة اللوز المحمص طالعة من فرن سلمى.
examples.trans: The aroma of toasted almonds is drifting out of Salma's oven.

examples.text: قشرة اللوز بتعطي تارت الليمون قرمشة طيبة.
examples.trans: An almond crust gives the lemon tart a delicious crunch.

meanings.note: The word 'محمصة' (محمصة) means 'محمصة'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: شوفوا آخر كلمة مش ملطخة عالزاوية: رشي شرائح لوز محمصة عالوجه.
examples.trans: Look at the last unsmudged word at the corner: scatter toasted sliced almonds on top.
This is محمصة.

meanings.note: The word 'عالوجه' (عالوجه) means 'عالوجه'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: شوفوا آخر كلمة مش ملطخة عالزاوية: رشي شرائح لوز محمصة عالوجه.
examples.trans: Look at the last unsmudged word at the corner: scatter toasted sliced almonds on top.
This is عالوجه.

meanings.note: The word 'معلقتين' (معلقتين) means 'معلقتين'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: معلقتين من العسل الدافي، وبرش برتقال، ورقائق لوز محمصة!
examples.trans: Two spoons of warm honey, grated orange zest, and toasted almond flakes!
This is معلقتين.

meanings.note: The word 'ورقائق' (ورقائق) means 'ورقائق'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: معلقتين من العسل الدافي، وبرش برتقال، ورقائق لوز محمصة!
examples.trans: Two spoons of warm honey, grated orange zest, and toasted almond flakes!
This is ورقائق.

meanings.note: Broken plural صواني ('serving trays' or 'oven baking pans').

examples.text: جهزنا تلات صواني خبز عشان تدخل الفرن الفجر.
examples.trans: We prepped three trays of bread to go into the oven at dawn.

examples.text: نور حملت صينية الشاي بالنعنع للساحة.
examples.trans: Nour carried the mint tea tray out to the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أرقام.

examples.trans: Here is your key, room number four.
Is there a phone number written on the paper?

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'three'; short form تلات (talaat) directly before a plural noun (تلات سنين 'three years').

examples.trans: Three years was a long time.
One, two, three!

meanings.note: The word 'دافية' (دافية) means 'دافية'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: استنتاج بسيط! صينية رقم واحد رح تاخد طبقة سكر وفانيليا دافية؛ هادا تشطيب كلاسيكي.
examples.trans: Simple deduction! Tin One gets a warm vanilla sugar glaze; that is a classic finish.
This is دافية.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'on, at, to'; before ال- it regularly contracts to عال- ('al- / 'a-).

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your forehead!
Say hello to Salma for me!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شباك.

examples.trans: The cake is cooling on the wire rack now.
We fitted an iron grille on the window.

meanings.note: The word 'الفرن—روحي' (الفرن—روحي) means 'الفرن—روحي'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: صينية رقم تلاتة لسه دافية على شبك الفرن—روحي ادهنيها هلق يا شيف!
examples.trans: Tin Three is still warm on the stove rack—go brush it right now, Chef!
This is الفرن—روحي.

meanings.note: The word 'ادهنيها' (ادهنيها) means 'ادهنيها'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: صينية رقم تلاتة لسه دافية على شبك الفرن—روحي ادهنيها هلق يا شيف!
examples.trans: Tin Three is still warm on the stove rack—go brush it right now, Chef!
This is ادهنيها.

meanings.note: The word 'هلق' (هلق) means 'هلق'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: راقبي الساعة يا نور—بعد أربعين دقيقة من هلق، لازم هدول الكيكات الصغيرة التلاتة يكونوا مثاليين.
examples.trans: Watch the clock, Nour—forty minutes from now, these three mini cakes must be perfect.
This is هلق.

meanings.note: Used across modern Jordanian kitchens and cafés for both male and female head chefs.

examples.text: الدفتر جاهز يا شيف سلمى، بشو نبلش؟
examples.trans: The clipboard is ready, Chef Salma—what do we start with?

examples.text: الشيف ذاق الشوربة وابتسم من أول معلقة.
examples.trans: The chef tasted the soup and smiled from the very first spoonful.

meanings.note: The word 'تتحركي' (تتحركي) means 'تتحركي'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: لا تتحركي عن مقعد البيانو يا سعاد؛ الكيكة الحقيقية رح تجهز بعد خمس دقايق!
examples.trans: Do not move from that piano bench, Suad; the real cake is five minutes away!
This is تتحركي.

meanings.note: Means 'about' (عن الزبدة), 'off / away from' (عن جبيني), and appears in عن جد ('really!') and عن إذنك ('excuse me').

examples.trans: I will carry the suitcase up for you.
I heard your voices about the butter!

meanings.note: Noun of place from ق-ع-د ('to sit'); names the seat of a chair or a garden bench.

examples.text: ارفع مقعد الكرسي شوي عشان يطوي معك.
examples.trans: Lift the chair seat slightly so it folds for you.

examples.text: في مقعد خشب طويل تحت شجرة الساحة.
examples.trans: There is a long wooden bench under the courtyard tree.

meanings.note: The word 'البيانو' (البيانو) means 'البيانو'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: لا تتحركي عن مقعد البيانو يا سعاد؛ الكيكة الحقيقية رح تجهز بعد خمس دقايق!
examples.trans: Do not move from that piano bench, Suad; the real cake is five minutes away!
This is البيانو.

meanings.note: The word 'سعاد' (سعاد) means 'سعاد'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: التلطيخة الزرقا مش مكون بنباع بسوق السبت يا سعاد!
examples.trans: Blue smudge is not an ingredient sold at the Saturday market, Suad!
This is سعاد.

meanings.note: The word 'الكيكة' (الكيكة) means 'الكيكة'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: خليني أشوف من نظاراتي: ادهني الكيكة الدافية بمعلقتين من... تلطيخة زرقا!
examples.trans: Let me look through my glasses: Brush warm cake with two spoons of... blue smudge!
This is الكيكة.

meanings.note: The word 'الحقيقية' (الحقيقية) means 'الحقيقية'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: لا تتحركي عن مقعد البيانو يا سعاد؛ الكيكة الحقيقية رح تجهز بعد خمس دقايق!
examples.trans: Do not move from that piano bench, Suad; the real cake is five minutes away!
This is الحقيقية.

meanings.note: Invariant spoken Levantine future marker placed before a subjunctive verb (without ب-).

examples.text: ضيفة غرفة أربعة رح تقعد كل الأسبوع.
examples.trans: Room four's guest will stay all week.

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day is not going to be boring!

meanings.note: The word 'تجهز' (تجهز) means 'تجهز'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: لا تتحركي عن مقعد البيانو يا سعاد؛ الكيكة الحقيقية رح تجهز بعد خمس دقايق!
examples.trans: Do not move from that piano bench, Suad; the real cake is five minutes away!
This is تجهز.

meanings.note: Means 'after' (بعد المطر) and with a future span 'in' (بعد أربعين دقيقة 'in forty minutes').

examples.trans: He arrives in forty minutes.
How lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: The word 'دقايق' (دقايق) means 'دقايق'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: معنا عشر دقايق بالزبط قبل ما تبرد الكيكة وترفض أي طبقة تلميع دافية!
examples.trans: We have exactly ten minutes before the cake cools down and rejects any warm glaze!
This is دقايق.

إلى.gloss: to; until (إلى اللقاء see you soon)

meanings.en: to; until (إلى اللقاء see you soon)
meanings.note: Appears in everyday speech inside warm set phrases such as إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again!').

examples.trans: See you soon, sir!
Goodbye and until next time.

meanings.note: The word 'اللقاء' (اللقاء) means 'اللقاء'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.trans: Goodbye!
This is اللقاء.

meanings.note: Passive participle for placed or put.

examples.trans: Here is the placed.
I like the placed.

meanings.note: Feminine adjective for old.

examples.trans: Here is the old (f).
I like the old (f).

meanings.note: Definite form of stone.

examples.trans: Here is the the stone.
I like the the stone.

meanings.note: Definite form of card.

examples.trans: Here is the the card.
I like the the card.

meanings.note: Definite form of old.

examples.trans: Here is the the old.
I like the the old.

meanings.note: Definite form of paper.

examples.trans: Here is the the paper.
I like the the paper.

meanings.note: Number five.

examples.trans: Here is the five.
I like the five.

meanings.note: Imperative plural verb for look.

examples.trans: Here is the look (pl).
I like the look (pl).

meanings.note: Definite form of a piece of paper.

examples.trans: Here is the the single paper.
I like the the single paper.

meanings.note: Adverb meaning still or not yet.

examples.trans: Here is the still / not yet.
I like the still / not yet.
